# CANDIDATE: TRENDLINE_BREAK_CALL_VETO_OOS_TEST

**Filed:** 2026-07-21
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** quality_gate
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Enabling the TRENDLINE_BREAK_CALL_VETO will block losing call entries on days where bearish market structure is confirmed (via 5m close-through-respected-ascending-support break), thereby improving call-side P&L without affecting the PUT side. The veto is expected to reduce call losses on losing days (particularly 5/07) while leaving all three PUT winner days untouched.

## Mechanism

The veto triggers when a 5m bar closes below a previously respected ascending support level (indicating a break of structure). When active, it suppresses all call entries for the remainder of the trading day. The veto resets at the start of each session and is evaluated independently for each bar. It does not interact with PUT entries or exits.

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+; $1K paper ~= 14% headline
2. **Sample bias:** Full 2025-01-02..2026-06-18 OPRA dataset (16 months); selection method = all available cached data; overfit risk mitigated by walk-forward and OOS testing (to be performed)
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (walk-forward held-out window pending)
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (top 3 J days validation pending)
5. **Failure modes:** 
   - Worst day: veto blocks call winners on misclassified bullish days (e.g., 5/01 or 5/04 if structure misread)
   - Max drawdown: increased if veto causes missed call recovery trades during choppy markets
   - Blow-up scenario: excessive veto triggering on weak structure signals turns call side into net loser
6. **Concentration:** unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest to compute top-5 days % of P&L
